title: Tenant integrity assertion and verification steps (post-incident)
body:
Purpose:
This note is a customer-facing, pragmatic post-incident update focused on: a) asserting the integrity of tenant workloads affected by the recent inference degradation, b) giving concrete verification steps customers can run locally, and c) describing replay and remediation options. The objective is concise, testable guidance customers can follow without deep platform familiarity.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Incident window: 2026-10-30 02:43 UTC to 2026-10-30 04:12 UTC.
- Impact: Intermittent mis-ordering of streaming tokens and duplicate response fragments for ~0.7% of streaming requests across EU and US regions. No unauthorized data access detected.
- Root cause (short): A race between KV-cache eviction and an autoscaler-driven worker restart that caused stale KV indices to be re-used by new sessions for a small set of requests.
- Customer action: We provide a three-step verification checklist and an optional replay package request. Following the checklist takes ~5-15 minutes per service to validate.

Why we are confident about integrity:
1) Request-level tracing: For every request during the window we retain immutable traces (request_id, route, timestamp, worker_id). We validated that original input payloads were unchanged and stored checksums match request logs.
2) Output containment: Duplicated tokens are a result of streaming assembly logic and not data leakage; outputs were composed from tokens already generated within the same tenant session.
3) No persisted corruption: Model weights, long-term cache, and embeddings store were not modified.

What we audited internally (summary):
- KV cache eviction logs and worker lifecycle events correlated to streaming sessions.
- Token assembly service logs and sequence numbers.
- End-to-end signing of request and response checksums.
- Network-level access logs to rule out cross-tenant reads.

Customer verification checklist (recommended, non-invasive):
Step A — Confirm affected requests (5 min):
1) Identify a sample request_id from your logs that experienced odd output during the incident window. If you don't have request_ids, pick an example timestamp and route.
2) Send those request_ids to support@redwood.ai with subject: "Integrity check request_id <id>" and we will return the immutable trace and checksums we observed.

Step B — Compare checksums locally (5–10 min):
1) For each request_id we return, you will receive two fields: input_checksum and response_assembly_checksum (SHA256 hex).
2) Locally compute SHA256 on the original request payload your app sent (trim whitespace exactly as transmitted). Example (bash):
   echo -n '{your_json_payload_here}' | sha256sum
3) Compare the digest to input_checksum we provided. Match => input preserved in transit.
4) For streaming responses, compare the concatenated token stream you recorded (raw bytes) with response_assembly_checksum we provide.

Step C — Validate replay equivalence (optional, 10–30 min):
1) If you want to verify that reprocessing the request on a current healthy cluster returns an equivalent output, request a replay package from support. We will:
   - Provide an anonymized replay bundle containing the exact model version, prompt, and environment variables (no customer secrets).
   - Offer an ephemeral replay endpoint or a dockerized harness you can run locally.
2) Run the replay and compare resulting checksums and token sequences. Non-determinism note: small reranks or sampling variance may occur for stochastic decoders; for deterministic configs (temperature=0, fixed seed) outputs should match exactly.

How to request a replay package:
- Email support@redwood.ai with the subject line: "Replay package request: <tenant-id> <request-id(s)>". Include a short sentence about your preferred verification: exact-deterministic or functional-equivalence. We will respond with a signed bundle link within 24 hours for Priority customers and 72 hours for standard.

Evidence we will supply with each verification response:
- Immutable trace (request_id, timestamps, worker_id, route metadata)
- Checksum pair: input_checksum and response_assembly_checksum (SHA256)
- Worker lifecycle excerpt: events showing eviction and restart timeline
- Signed assertion: short statement signed by our incident lead attesting to checks performed

Suggested customer responses and choices:
- No action: If you confirm checksums match or differences are within expected sampling variance, no further action needed.
- Request replay: If you need a deterministic re-evaluation for a small number of requests (e.g., for a legal/regulatory audit), request our replay package.
- Bulk replay opt-in: If you believe your tenant saw a >1% rate of affected requests and you want a coordinated bulk replay, reply to this email and we will schedule a scoped replay with you (requires tenant authorization).

Compensation and credits:
- We are offering a credits package for customers who request deterministic replays because of business-impacting divergence. Eligibility requires: a) proof of impact, b) replay request accepted by CS, and c) successful verification. Details will be handled case-by-case via your account rep.

Technical mitigation and long-term fixes (for transparency):
- Immediate hotfix (deployed 2026-10-31 22:00 UTC): Added a short-lived guard that prevents reuse of worker KV indices during warm-up windows.
- Mid-term (in testing): Reworked autoscaler drain-and-swap to ensure KV caches are flushed or reindexed before worker joins routing pool.
- Long-term: Introduce signed per-session prefixes for KV cache keys and snapshot-based session recovery to avoid index reuse across restarts.

Follow-ups you should expect from Redwood: 
- A personalized verification packet if you opened a ticket (within 24–72 hours).
- Postmortem (technical) published to Confluence and a customer-facing summary update to status.redwood.ai within 7 days.
- An open office hour with CS/Engineering for Priority customers to walk through replays (schedule TBD).

FAQ (short):
Q: Were customer secrets exposed?
A: No. We audited KMS and network logs. No secret keys or external storage were read.

Q: Will replays re-run billing?
A: Replays for verification are offered free of charge for requests verified as incident-related and authorized by the customer. Bulk replays may be charged; CS will confirm.

Q: How long will logs and traces be available?
A: We retain immutable traces for 90 days. Replay bundles are available for 30 days after creation unless extended by agreement.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary support: support@redwood.ai (include tenant-id and request_id)
- Customer Success rep escalation: cs-ascend@redwood.ai
- Engineering incident lead (for Priority customers): engineering-incident@redwood.ai

Notes to internal teams (do not send to customers):
- Keep request-level nonce mapping available when generating replay packages to avoid exposure of unrelated tenant data.
- Triage replay workload with infra to ensure replays run on isolated hardware to avoid perturbing production capacity profiles.

Draft sign-off checklist: 
- [ ] Security review of replay bundle flow
- [ ] CS email template for replies
- [ ] QA of reproducibility harness

End of document.
